Note that plugging in $x=1$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-11}{4{x}^{3}-4} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{[5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-11]^{′}}{[4{x}^{3}-4]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{15{x}^{2}+12x}{12{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{15(1)^{2}+12(1)}{12(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{15+12}{12} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
